brief: Goldman's weekly positioning wrap (Saboureault's Positioning Mondays plus Stankard's Equity Positioning and Key Levels) finds the prime book adding gross (308.7%, 60th percentile) while cutting net (75.9%, 10th percentile), so funds want exposure but still lean bearish with the S&P near a record. The US fundamental long/short ratio hit a five-year low. Info Tech flipped from the most-bought sector in 4 of 5 weeks to the most-sold after OpenAI revenue headlines hit an already record-overweight Magnificent 7 position, pushing AI versus the rest to a 10-point gap; Goldman now tells clients to buy the laggards. Money rotated into Industrials (fastest pace since January) and out of Staples, Health Care and Biotech. CTAs have sold roughly $81bn (two-thirds of their length) over a month, mostly outside the US, and are now "on target" with limited further flow unless a trend reasserts; S&P pivots sit at 7,704/7,493/7,012 against a 7,811 close. Buybacks stay in blackout but should reopen after bank earnings. Breadth (Dot-Com lows) and implied correlation (near record lows) show a narrow market; the bull case needs oil (Houthi strikes near Saudi capital) and rates (a hawkish Warsh) to recede.
